- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and slow downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0 to +0.20), model underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 2-5% for next 3-5 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days ahead) — add 1-3% buffer to short-term forecasts if sentiment is stable or mildly bullish.  
- When sentiment turns from negative to positive (e.g., +0.20+), model lags in recognizing the shift — delay forecast adjustment by 1-2 days and increase slope gently.  
- In low-volatility periods, model over-smooths — allow 1-2% noise in forecast to reflect sentiment-driven volatility spikes.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to forecast lower than true — add 2-5% upward bias to compensate for sentiment drag.
